transcript:
User: yeah.
Agent: Yeah, I am—I’m Linda, an AI assistant on Jay’s team at Dialux, and I help with the intro and getting a quick walkthrough set up. What made you call today?
User: dunno, whatever's fine.
Agent: Got it… when a call comes in and you’re tied up, who’s usually picking up the phone?
User: dunno. maybe someone.
Agent: Makes sense—when “maybe someone” doesn’t pick up, do those calls usually go to voicemail?
User: maybe. voicemail's fine.
Agent: Got it—when it does go to voicemail, do people usually leave a message, or do they just hang up and call the next company?
User: dunno, sometimes voicemail, sometimes not.
Agent: Right—roughly how many calls a week do you think end up going to voicemail?
User: dunno, maybe a few.
Agent: Got it—what kind of business is this for?
User: it's fine. dunno, whatever's fine really.
Agent: Mhm—if you had to label it, are you more like a local service business (plumbing/HVAC/electrical), a shop, or an office-type business?
User: dunno. maybe local, maybe office. whatever fits best.
Agent: Got it—are the calls you get mostly people trying to book something (like an appointment/estimate), or are they more general questions?
User: dunno, maybe both. whatever they need.
Agent: Makes sense—when those “book something” calls come in and nobody grabs them, are you okay with them landing in voicemail, or do you want them getting scheduled right then?
User: maybe voicemail, maybe schedule. whatever works.
Agent: Got it—when a call goes to voicemail and they don’t leave a message, do you feel like you’re losing some of those to a competitor?
User: maybe. dunno. voicemail's fine, whatever.
Agent: Got it—if voicemail’s fine, what would you want to be different about your calls, if anything?
User: dunno. maybe clearer. whatever. not too long.
Agent: Got it—when you say “clearer,” do you mean a shorter voicemail message and fewer back-and-forth calls?
User: maybe. dunno. just not too long. whatever's fine.
Agent: Got it—when calls hit voicemail, do you want a short message that just takes their name/number, or one that also asks what they need so you know how to call them back?
User: dunno. maybe short. whatever's fine, just simple.
Agent: Got it—when those “few a week” go to voicemail and it’s short/simple, are you still getting back to them the same day most of the time?
User: dunno. maybe. depends on the day. whatever's fine, really.
Agent: Got it—what’s the main reason it depends: are you just busy on jobs, or is it more that there isn’t a consistent person assigned to return those messages?
User: dunno. maybe both. whatever works that day. sure, depends on who's free.
Agent: Got it—so it really comes down to whoever’s free, and that’s when calls can slip to voicemail. Would you want those missed calls handled automatically so you’re not relying on someone being available?
User: maybe. dunno, sometimes voicemail. whatever's fine, just depends.
Agent: Got it—it depends. If you could pick just one, would you rather those missed calls get a short voicemail message, or get handled so the caller can lock in a time right then?
User: dunno. maybe voicemail. whatever fits. sometimes schedule. sure, whatever.
Agent: Got it—so a short voicemail most of the time, and scheduling sometimes. Is there any point in the day—like after-hours or when you’re busiest—where you really don’t want calls going to voicemail?
User: maybe. dunno. whenever's fine. just avoid peak times. whatever works best.
Agent: Got it—peak times are the big one. What are those peak times for you—mornings, lunch, after-hours, or something else?
User: dunno. maybe mornings. whatever's busiest. lunch too, sometimes after-hours. just avoid those. sure, whenever's least busy.
Agent: Got it—mornings, lunch, and sometimes after-hours. In those peak windows, are those mostly new people calling to book, or existing customers calling with questions?
User: dunno. maybe both. sometimes new, sometimes existing. whatever fits that day, really. sure, could be either.
Agent: Got it—both, depending on the day. If we could take peak-time calls, keep it short and simple, and either capture the details or schedule when needed, would you want to see how that works?
User: sure, maybe. dunno if that’s needed. whatever works for now. maybe later, not too sure yet.
Agent: Totally fair—sounds like it’s not urgent. What would have to start happening for it to feel “needed” sooner (more missed calls, losing bookings, staff stretched, something else)?
User: dunno. maybe more calls missed, bookings lost. whatever happens, happens. not sure, depends on how busy it gets.
Agent: Got it—so if it starts getting busier and you’re missing more calls and bookings, that’s when it matters. What’s the busiest season or month for you?
User: dunno. maybe spring, maybe fall. could be summer too. whatever's busiest that year. depends on demand.
Agent: Got it—so you’ve got seasonal spikes where it can get busy fast. When that hits, what’s the one thing you’d want handled automatically: capturing every caller’s details, or actually booking them onto the schedule?
User: dunno. maybe capturing details. whatever's easiest. sure, maybe bookings too. depends on the day, really.
Agent: Got it—capturing details is the priority, with booking as a nice-to-have on busy days. Has anyone ever showed you the math on what a few missed calls a week can cost you?
User: dunno. maybe. sure, heard some. whatever it costs, happens. not too worried, really.
Agent: Got it—you’re not too worried right now. Mind if I do a super quick 30‑second calculation using your numbers, just so you know what “a few a week” looks like in dollars?
User: dunno. maybe later. whatever's fine. not too sure about that now. just depends, really.
Agent: Got it—timing-wise, it sounds like this is more of a “when we get busier” thing. When do you expect the next busy stretch to start?
User: dunno. maybe spring or summer. whenever's busiest that year. just depends on demand. whatever happens, happens.
Agent: Got it—spring or summer, depending on demand. If we kept it really simple: about how many calls per week do you think hit voicemail in those busy weeks—10, 20, 30?
User: dunno. maybe 10, maybe 30. whatever happens those weeks. sure, could be any number really. depends on demand.
Agent: Got it—let’s use 20 a week as a middle number. Of those missed calls, what percentage do you think would’ve booked if someone answered—like 25%, 50%, 75%?
User: dunno. maybe 50%. sure, could be higher. whatever works for now. just depends on the calls, really.
Agent: Got it—let’s use 50% for a clean estimate. What’s your average job value when someone does book—are we talking $200, $500, $1,000?
